name: Native IMASM-Numeral Mapping

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Z2 topological invariant that prevents continuous deformation of the numeral state to a trivial zero without crossing a phase boundary.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before any digit or magnitude is assigned, representing the empty set of values.

⊣.justification: The closed network structure that contains the full bulk content of the numeral system, unifying surface and interior.

≻.justification: The forward morphism that increases the count or moves the system toward a higher magnitude state.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism that decreases the count or descends toward a lower magnitude state.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of digits to form a multi-digit numeral, enforcing geometric constraints on binding.

⊙.justification: The self-referential state where the system is at the threshold with scale-free correlations, recognizing its own value.

∈.justification: The split of a numeral state into two arms based on parity: even (affirmative) and odd (negative) branches.

∋.justification: The reconstitution of the parity arms into a single state, reflecting asymmetric distribution of counts across the reaction boundary.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where the numeral is constructively proven to be even.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the numeral is constructively refuted as even, establishing oddness.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where both even and odd parities are held simultaneously, maintaining broken orientational symmetry.

⊡.justification: The permanent, append-only fixation of a numeral value, preventing continuous deformation to a trivial state.

phase_2.fuse_result: a resolved numeral state with defined parity or a contradiction if both hold
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The state before any numeral is defined, containing no digits or magnitude.
phase_3.true_description: The state where a numeral is constructively proven to exist and hold a specific value.
phase_3.false_description: The state where a numeral is constructively refuted or negated.
phase_3.both_description: The state where a numeral holds both a value and its negation simultaneously, a chiral superposition.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the system to the void_numeral state, establishing the empty set of values.
Establish the topological_boundary that contains the full bulk content of the numeral system.
Apply increment_magnitude to move the system toward a higher magnitude state.
Compose digits via digit_composition to form a multi-digit numeral.
Branch the numeral state into parity_branch, separating even and odd possibilities.
Evaluate the even_parity arm to affirm constructive truth of evenness.
Evaluate the odd_parity arm to refute evenness and establish oddness.
Hold the chiral_superposition state where both parities are simultaneously active.
Rejoin the parity arms via stoichiometric_rejoin to a single resolved state.
Enter the critical_state where the system recognizes its own value at the threshold.
Apply decrement_magnitude to descend toward a lower magnitude state.
Fix the current numeral value as an immutable_record, preventing deformation.
Chain the fixed record with subsequent operations to maintain high-fidelity binding.
Re-anchor the system to the topological_boundary to ensure closure.
